title: Squared paper, ruler
subject: Geography

intro: Lesson 18: Home fieldwork: where does our kitchen food come from?. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Our question
points: Where does our kitchen food come from?

bullets: Bar chart: one bar per continent

parts.text: So most food came from abroad

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: Most of our food (12 of 20) came from abroad, though the UK was the biggest single source.

keywords.def: collecting information yourself, outside the classroom
a chart using bars to show amounts

questions.q: What do you write if the label only says 'packed in UK'?

questions.a: IIII II (a bundle of five and two)

questions.q: What must a bar chart have?
Core: Using your own kitchen data (or the sample data sheet), make a tally chart and a bar chart by continent.
questions.a: An accurate tally and a titled, labelled bar chart

questions.q: Extend: Write a conclusion: 'Most of our food comes from... because...'
questions.a: A conclusion matching the chart with a reason

questions.q: Stretch: How could you make the results more reliable?
questions.a: Check more foods, or a second kitchen, and record unknowns honestly

questions.q: In the example, how many foods came from abroad?
questions.a: B) 12. 20 foods minus 8 from the UK leaves 12 from abroad.
Answer from the pupil's own data with a reason
